title: QUIC RFC 9000 Client 0-RTT Handshake Value Supersession Policy Verification
verification_method: Focused S7P4P1 requirement-home tests over client use of server handshake values and default fallback for transport parameters that must not be remembered for 0-RTT, plus Release build, regenerated QUIC coverage triage, SpecTrace JSON validation, full Release test suite, and whitespace diff checking.
scope: This verification covers the internal client policy that resolves prohibited remembered transport parameters from the new handshake values or defaults.
expected_result: The focused tests show remembered prohibited values are ignored when the server provides new handshake values, and default or absent values are used when the server omits those handshake values.
procedure: Run the focused S7P4P1 requirement-home filter.
Run the full Release test suite without rebuilding.
Check the resulting diff for whitespace errors.
preconditions: The client remembered transport-parameter subset excludes prohibited remembered values.
The runtime's public early-data admission remains closed.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This verification does not claim updated-value use in 0-RTT packets, server protocol-violation handling, public early-data APIs, TLS early_data extension admission wiring, anti-replay behavior, or application-data delivery.

status_summary: Passed locally on 2026-05-06. The Release build passed with 0 warnings and 0 errors, the focused S7P4P1 filter passed 25/25, regenerated coverage triage marks RFC9000-S7-4-1-P4-S2-R01 trace_clean and reports 1,270 of 1,771 QUIC requirements trace-clean overall, core SpecTrace JSON validation passed for 454 artifacts, the full Release no-build suite passed 4,489/4,489, and git diff --check returned exit code 0 with line-ending warnings only.
